'''Maria Manuel Mota''' is a Portuguese [[malariologist]] and executive director of the [[Instituto de Medicina Molecular]] João Lobo Antunes, [[Lisbon]].

== Education ==
Maria Mota, a native of [[Vila Nova de Gaia]], graduated from her undergraduate degree in Biology in 1992 and received her master's degree in immunology in 1994 from the [[University of Porto]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.edctpforum2018.org/en/content/programme/speakers/maria-mota.html|title=Ninth EDCTP Forum 2018 – Professor Maria Mota|website=www.edctpforum2018.org|access-date=2019-01-04}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.dn.pt/sociedade/interior/a-investigadora-8688850.html|title=A investigadora|last=Tavares|first=Pedro|date=7 August 2017|website=www.dn.pt|language=pt|access-date=2019-01-04}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=http://upmagazine-tap.com/en/pt_artigos/the-factor-x-2/|title=Up Magazine – TAP Portugal » Maria Manuel Mota — The factor X|last=Dias|first=Ana Sousa|date=1 Oct 2009|website=upmagazine-tap.com|access-date=2019-01-05|archive-date=2019-02-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190224002159/http://upmagazine-tap.com/en/pt_artigos/the-factor-x-2/|url-status=dead}}</ref> She received her PhD in molecular parasitology in 1998 from [[University College London]], working at the affiliated [[National Institute for Medical Research]] with Will Jarra and Anthony Holder.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://imm.medicina.ulisboa.pt/en/investigacao/labs/mota-lab/|title=iMM Lisboa — Mota, Maria M. Lab|website=imm.medicina.ulisboa.pt|access-date=2019-01-04|archive-date=2019-03-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190320210117/https://imm.medicina.ulisboa.pt/en/investigacao/labs/mota-lab/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Career ==
Mota moved to the [[United States]] after her PhD to postdoc at the [[New York University Medical Center]] in the lab of Victor Nussenzweig.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wehi.edu.au/professor-maria-mota-university-lisbon|title=Professor Maria Mota – University of Lisbon|last=Research|first=The Walter and Eliza Hall Institute of Medical|date=2015-02-09|website=Walter and Eliza Hall Institute of Medical Research|access-date=2019-01-04}}</ref> In 2002 she set up her first research group at [[Instituto Gulbenkian de Ciência]], [[Oeiras, Portugal]]. In 2005 Mota was made a professor at the [[University of Lisbon]]. She has been executive director at the Instituto de Medicina Molecular João Lobo Antunes (iMM) in Lisbon since 2014, and still leads the Biology and Physiology of Malaria research group.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Mota|first=Maria M.|date=2016-06-01|title=Maria Mota: The Pleasure of Discovery|journal=Trends in Parasitology|language=English|volume=32|issue=6|pages=429–430|doi=10.1016/j.pt.2016.01.003|issn=1471-5007|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=":1" />

In 2016 Mota was elected a member of [[European Molecular Biology Organization|EMBO]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.embo.org/news/press-releases/2016/58-life-science-researchers-elected-as-new-embo-members|title=58 life science researchers elected as new EMBO Members|date=23 May 2016|website=EMBO|access-date=2019-01-04|archive-date=2016-08-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160815104046/http://www.embo.org/news/press-releases/2016/58-life-science-researchers-elected-as-new-embo-members|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://people.embo.org/profile/maria-m-mota|title=Find people in the EMBO Communities|website=people.embo.org|access-date=2019-01-04}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2016-05/e-5ls052316.php|title=58 life science researchers elected as new EMBO Members|website=EurekAlert!|access-date=2019-01-04}}</ref> She is a visiting professor of immunology and infectious disease at the [[Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health]] in the lab of [[Dyann Wirth]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hsph.harvard.edu/maria-mota/|title=Maria Mota|website=Harvard TH Chan School of Public Health|access-date=2019-01-05}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hsph.harvard.edu/wirth-lab/wirth-lab-th-chan-school/|title=Wirth Lab – Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health|last1=Boston|first1=677 Huntington Avenue|last2=Ma 02115 +1495‑1000|date=2015-05-06|website=Wirth Lab|access-date=2019-01-05}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://connects.catalyst.harvard.edu/Profiles/display/Person/93539|title=Maria Mota {{!}} Harvard Catalyst Profiles {{!}} Harvard Catalyst|website=connects.catalyst.harvard.edu|access-date=2019-01-05}}</ref>

In addition to her career as a researcher, Mota was founder and vice-president of the Portuguese science public outreach organisation ''[[:pt:Associação Viver a Ciência|Associação Viver a Ciência]]''.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":5">{{Cite web|url=http://www.viveraciencia.org/pt/a-vac/pages/maria-mota-premio-pessoa|title=Maria Mota – Prémio Pessoa|website=www.viveraciencia.org|access-date=2019-01-05}}</ref>

== Research ==
Throughout her career Mota has researched the molecular biology of malaria infection, especially regarding host-pathogen interactions. Although she studies molecular interactions her research has linked these to grander host factors which influence infection, such as nutrition status and circadian rhythms.

Mota was the lead researcher of the first study to demonstrate that malaria parasites, when they enter the liver early in infection, enter and traverse through multiple liver cells before finding a cell that they stay in for replication.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Rodríguez|first1=Ana|last2=Nussenzweig|first2=Victor|last3=Nussenzweig|first3=Ruth S.|last4=Frevert|first4=Ute|last5=Hafalla|first5=Julius C. R.|last6=Vanderberg|first6=Jerome P.|last7=Pradel|first7=Gabriele|last8=Mota|first8=Maria M.|date=2001-01-05|title=Migration of Plasmodium Sporozoites Through Cells Before Infection|journal=Science|volume=291|issue=5501|pages=141–144|doi=10.1126/science.291.5501.141|issn=1095-9203|pmid=11141568|bibcode=2001Sci...291..141M}}</ref> This work was based on a serendipitous discovery made from a conversation between Mota and [[Ana Rodriguez (Scientist)|Ana Rodriguez]] in a lift, about an old film Rodriguez had from a previous research project.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Enserink|first=Martin|date=2001-01-05|title=Old Movie Spawns a New Discovery|journal=Science|volume=291|issue=5501|pages=24–25|doi= 10.1126/science.10.1126/SCIENCE.291.5501.24 <!-- Valid DOI-->|issn=1095-9203|pmid=11191991|s2cid=35673789}}</ref> The work was another example of collaboration between Victor and [[Ruth Nussenzweig]].

Mota’s research has often investigated the liver stage of malaria, an oft-forgotten stage of the parasite, but an important one since it is the first stage of infection after mosquito bite. Mysteriously immunity to this part of the malaria life cycle is very poor. Mota was involved in a study which showed that this is partially a consequence of the repression of [[Dendritic cell]]s in the liver, which normally activate [[T cell]]s and present them with the molecular targets of the infection.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Rodriguez|first1=Ana|last2=Mota|first2=Maria M.|last3=Ocaña-Morgner|first3=Carlos|date=2003-01-20|title=Malaria Blood Stage Suppression of Liver Stage Immunity by Dendritic Cells|journal=Journal of Experimental Medicine|volume=197|issue=2|pages=143–151|doi=10.1084/jem.20021072|issn=1540-9538|pmc=2193811|pmid=12538654}}</ref> However she later showed that the liver does possess an active [[innate immune system]] response.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mota|first1=Maria M.|last2=Barchet|first2=Winfried|last3=Fitzgerald|first3=Katherine A.|last4=Rice|first4=Charles M.|last5=Vigário|first5=Ana M.|last6=Pichlmair|first6=Andreas|last7=Superti-Furga|first7=Giulio|last8=Kappe|first8=Stefan H.|last9=Coelho|first9=Luis P.|date=January 2014|title=Host-cell sensors for Plasmodium activate innate immunity against liver-stage infection|journal=Nature Medicine|volume=20|issue=1|pages=47–53|doi=10.1038/nm.3424|issn=1546-170X|pmc=4096771|pmid=24362933}}</ref> Malaria cells further protect themselves from destruction by the liver cells themselves (through [[Autophagy]]) by binding the autophagy factor [[Microtubule-associated protein]] light chain 3 (LC3).<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mota|first1=Maria M.|last2=Mair|first2=Gunnar R.|last3=Figueira|first3=Tiago N.|last4=Zuzarte-Luís|first4=Vanessa|last5=Vera|first5=Iset M.|last6=Beatty|first6=Wandy|last7=Mello-Vieira|first7=João|last8=Mancio-Silva|first8=Liliana|last9=Enguita|first9=Francisco J.|date=January 2018|title=Plasmodium UIS3 sequesters host LC3 to avoid elimination by autophagy in hepatocytes|journal=Nature Microbiology|volume=3|issue=1|pages=17–25|doi=10.1038/s41564-017-0054-x|issn=2058-5276|pmc=5739284|pmid=29109477}}</ref> This research opens up a new therapeutic target for malaria drugs.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2017-11/idmm-ctb110617.php|title=Could this be malaria's Achilles heel?|website=EurekAlert!|access-date=2019-01-05}}</ref>

Mota’s own research group showed that an ongoing blood stage infection inhibits a new malaria liver stage (i.e. repressing [[superinfection]] from a later mosquito bite). This works through the action of [[hepcidin]], which is upregulated during malaria infection and diverts iron away from liver cells, starving a new malaria infection of an essential nutrient.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mota|first1=Maria M.|last2=Drakesmith|first2=Hal|last3=Newbold|first3=Chris I.|last4=Roy|first4=Cindy|last5=Sullivan|first5=David|last6=Epiphanio|first6=Sabrina|last7=Gonçalves|first7=Lígia A.|last8=Armitage|first8=Andrew E.|last9=Recker|first9=Mario|date=June 2011|title=Host-mediated regulation of superinfection in malaria|journal=Nature Medicine|volume=17|issue=6|pages=732–737|doi=10.1038/nm.2368|issn=1546-170X|pmc=4200394|pmid=21572427}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mota|first1=Maria M.|last2=Drakesmith|first2=Hal|last3=Portugal|first3=Sílvia|date=2011-12-01|title=Superinfection in malaria: Plasmodium shows its iron will|journal=EMBO Reports|volume=12|issue=12|pages=1233–1242|doi=10.1038/embor.2011.213|issn=1469-3178|pmc=3245699|pmid=22081142}}</ref>

In 2017 Mota’s team published research indicating that malaria parasites are able to sense the nutritional status of their host and correspondingly alter their growth rates. 30% calorie restriction diets of laboratory mice lead to a reduction in growth rate of ''[[Plasmodium berghei]]'' parasites in the mice blood. A malaria [[kinase]] protein, KIN, was found to be involved in sensing host nutritional status, as when it was [[Gene knockout|genetically knocked-out]] of the parasites they did not respond to host calorie restriction.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sanger.ac.uk/news/view/malaria-parasites-able-sense-their-hosts-calorie-intake|title=Malaria parasites able to sense their host's calorie intake|last=www-core (webteam)|website=www.sanger.ac.uk|access-date=2019-01-05}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dn.pt/sociedade/interior/maria-mota-faz-descoberta-que-pode-ser-chave-para-sobreviver-a-malaria-8615622.html|title=Maria Mota faz descoberta que pode ser chave para sobreviver à malária|website=www.dn.pt|language=pt|access-date=2019-01-05}}</ref><ref name=":4" /> These results match evidence from human infections, as doctors had noticed that malaria infections sometimes get more severe after hospitalisation and improved feeding of malnourished patients.<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal|last1=Mota|first1=Maria M.|last2=Billker|first2=Oliver|last3=Llinás|first3=Manuel|last4=Tewari|first4=Rita|last5=Baena-Gonzalez|first5=Elena|last6=Adamo|first6=Mattia|last7=Crozet|first7=Pierre|last8=MacPherson|first8=Cameron Ross|last9=Gomes|first9=Ana Rita|date=July 2017|title=Nutrient sensing modulates malaria parasite virulence|journal=Nature|volume=547|issue=7662|pages=213–216|doi=10.1038/nature23009|issn=1476-4687|pmc=5511512|pmid=28678779|bibcode=2017Natur.547..213M}}</ref>

== Awards ==
In 2003 Mota was given a Young Investigator Award by [[European Molecular Biology Organization|EMBO]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.embo.org/documents/news/facts_figures/EMBO_annual_report_2003.pdf|title=EMBO Annual Report 2003|website=www.embo.org|access-date=2019-01-04}}</ref> More funding came from a [[European Science Foundation]] Young Investigator award in 2004.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Project descriptions of the EURYI award winners 2004 |url=http://archives.esf.org/coordinating-research/euryi/awards/2004.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190617104429/http://archives.esf.org/coordinating-research/euryi/awards/2004.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 17, 2019 |access-date=2019-01-04 |website=European Science Foundation}}</ref>

In 2005 Mota was appointed Commander of the [[Order of Prince Henry]] (''Comendadora da Ordem do Infante D. Henrique''), a national honour of [[Portugal]].<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ordens.presidencia.pt/?idc=153&list=1|title=ENTIDADES NACIONAIS AGRACIADAS COM ORDENS PORTUGUESAS – Página Oficial das Ordens Honoríficas Portuguesas|website=www.ordens.presidencia.pt|access-date=2019-01-04}}</ref>

She was honored with the [[Pessoa Prize|Prémio Pessoa Prize]] in 2013, given to Portuguese citizens who contribute significantly to the arts or sciences. Mota is one of the youngest recipients of the prestigious award.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":5" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.publico.pt/2013/12/13/ciencia/noticia/premio-pessoa-2013-atribuido-a-1616177|title=Maria Mota, galardoada com o Pessoa 2013: "Este prémio é para a minha geração de cientistas"|last=Ferreira|first=Nicolau|website=PÚBLICO|language=pt|access-date=2019-01-04}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://news.medicina.ulisboa.pt/en/2014/06/15/maria-mota-recebe-premio-pessoa-e-lanca-alerta-para-decisores-politicos/|title=Maria Mota was awarded the Pessoa Prize and leaves an alert for political decision-makers « News@fmul News@fmul|access-date=2019-01-04}}</ref>

In November 2017 she was awarded the Pfizer Prize for her work in the area of malaria.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.jornaldenegocios.pt/economia/saude/detalhe/premios-pfizer-distinguem-trabalhos-sobre-cataratas-malaria-e-parkinson|title=Prémios Pfizer distinguem trabalhos sobre cataratas, malária e Parkinson|website=www.jornaldenegocios.pt|language=pt-pt|access-date=2019-01-05}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://news.medicina.ulisboa.pt/en/2017/11/21/premios-pfizer-2017-para-descobertas-para-visao-malaria-e-parkinson/|title=2017 Pfizer Awards for Discoveries in the fields of Vision, Malaria and Parkinson's « News@fmul News@fmul|access-date=2019-01-05}}</ref>

In November 2018 she received the mid-career Sanofi-[[Pasteur Institute|Institut Pasteur]] prize, worth 150 thousand euros.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/nous-soutenir/comment-nous-soutenir/entreprises-fondations/ils-nous-soutiennent/sanofi-institut-pasteur-awards/2018-award-winners-0|title=The 2018 award winners|date=2018-10-15|website=Institut Pasteur|language=fr|access-date=2019-01-04}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.publico.pt/2018/11/15/ciencia/noticia/investigadora-maria-mota-vence-premio-1851200|title=Investigadora Maria Mota vence (mais um) prémio|date=15 Nov 2018|website=Publico|language=Portuguese|access-date=4 Jan 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://observador.pt/2018/11/15/maria-manuel-mota-nao-e-um-balurdio-de-dinheiro-mas-e-livre/|title=Maria Manuel Mota: "Não é um balúrdio de dinheiro, mas é livre"|last=Novais|first=Vera|website=Observador|language=pt-PT|access-date=2019-01-04}}</ref>
